continuity.campaign_development: February 59 BCE: Valerius continued the planned invasion beyond the outer bandit estates and pushed into the inner estate network. A fortified storehouse produced another costly fight, local smallholders began approaching the Roman lines with geographic and human-network information, and Marcus Claudius Marcellus maintained an established political correspondence with the expedition. A surprise night strike disrupted a supply movement, demonstrating that the remaining bandit fighters could still operate around Roman-held ground. The month ended with Valerius deeper inside the network and better informed, but with fewer soldiers, lower supplies, greater exhaustion, slightly reduced readiness and more strained local relations.

event_variety_policy.rule: Do not make every event about the same subject. Prefer distinct news dimensions supported by current state: military operations, intelligence, logistics, political relationships, economic/property activity, social/local developments, personal developments, geography, and reactions. Variety must arise from simulation context and must not be fabricated solely to fill slots.
